page.notes: Marginal note at right, beside "Et": "1 Horat. 2. Epist. 1." (mark 1 in the text). Greek passages (2 Tim. 4:3, Matth. 23:10, Jac. 3:1, 1 Pet. 5:1) are printed in a heavy, partly smudged face; the accents and some letters are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. Long s was normalised to plain s. The "Κνηθόμενοι" word and the first Greek phrase are read from a blurred line. The dash rules after "nobiscum sentit" and "odio quibus se inimicos profitentur" are printed as leaders and are kept as dashes. The line "Ne multi estote" begins a new paragraph by a number, so it is a paragraph, not a heading.
